artifacts.title: OpenAI's first Super Bowl ad: 'The Intelligence Age'
artifacts.quote: We're at the dawn of the intelligence age, and you can participate today
artifacts.speaker: Kate Rouch (OpenAI CMO)
artifacts.summary: OpenAI's debut Super Bowl LIX spot was a 60-second pointillist animation placing ChatGPT alongside humanity's great inventions; Business Insider put the cost at about $14M. OpenAI said Sora was used only for brainstorming and humans made the final animation.
artifacts.lesson: When you are the AI company, having humans make your ad is the message.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: run a Super Bowl ad

artifacts.title: Anthropic's Super Bowl ads: 'A Time and a Place'
artifacts.quote: Ads are coming to AI. But not to Claude.
artifacts.speaker: Anthropic (ad tagline)
artifacts.summary: Anthropic's four-spot campaign ('Betrayal', 'Treachery', 'Violation', 'Deception') showed chatbot answers derailing into product pitches; two spots ran before and during Super Bowl LX on Feb 8, 2026, right after OpenAI said it would test ads in ChatGPT's free and Go tiers.
artifacts.lesson: Attack ads work best when they attack a rival's business model, not its product.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: run a Super Bowl ad attacking a rival

artifacts.title: Altman responds to Anthropic's ad campaign
artifacts.quote: I wonder why Anthropic would go for something so clearly dishonest.
artifacts.speaker: Sam Altman
artifacts.summary: Days before the game, Altman posted a long X thread saying the ads were funny and that he laughed, but calling them dishonest and arguing Anthropic serves 'an expensive product to rich people'; coverage noted the response amplified the campaign.
artifacts.lesson: Responding to a rival's ad is buying them a second airing for free.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: rival runs an attack ad and you respond publicly

artifacts.title: OpenAI's second Super Bowl ad: Codex
artifacts.speaker: OpenAI (ad end line)
artifacts.summary: OpenAI returned with a 60-second Super Bowl LX spot for Codex, shot on film with real people, ending 'You Can Just Build Things'; it aired in a game where Google, Meta, Amazon and Anthropic also ran AI ads.
artifacts.lesson: Once every rival buys the Super Bowl, the slot buys parity, not distinction.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: run a Super Bowl ad when 3+ rivals also do

artifacts.title: Google pulls 'Dear Sydney' Gemini Olympics ad
artifacts.quote: While the ad tested well before airing, given the feedback, we have decided to phase the ad out of our Olympics rotation.
artifacts.speaker: Google
artifacts.summary: The spot showed a father having Gemini draft his daughter's fan letter to hurdler Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone; after heavy rotation in the first week of the Paris Olympics, backlash over outsourcing a child's self-expression forced Google to pull it.
artifacts.lesson: Never market AI as a replacement for the human moment the audience cherishes.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: AI-generated ad campaign / TV ad depicting AI replacing personal expression

artifacts.title: Artisan's 'Stop Hiring Humans' billboards
artifacts.speaker: Artisan (billboard copy)
artifacts.summary: YC-backed Artisan plastered San Francisco with billboards like 'Stop Hiring Humans' and 'Artisans won't complain about work-life balance' for its AI sales agents; the public reaction was overwhelmingly hostile and the CEO defended it as deliberate provocation.
artifacts.lesson: Rage-bait buys awareness at the price of being the face of everyone's job anxiety.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: provocative billboard campaign about replacing workers

artifacts.title: Friend.com's $1M NYC subway takeover
artifacts.quote: The picture of the billboard is the billboard
artifacts.speaker: Avi Schiffmann (Friend CEO)
artifacts.summary: Friend spent about $1M on 11,000+ subway car ads, 1,000 platform posters and 130 urban panels, Outfront's biggest NYC subway campaign of the year; New Yorkers defaced them ('AI wouldn't care if you lived or died'), and the CEO embraced the vandalism as earned media while the pendant had sold ~3,000 units.
artifacts.lesson: Backlash can be the campaign, but only if you never needed the public to like you.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: out-of-home ad blitz with low public trust in AI

artifacts.title: ChatGPT launches as a 'low-key research preview'
artifacts.summary: OpenAI framed ChatGPT internally as a 'low-key research preview' with no marketing push (staff later made it a laptop sticker); it passed 1M users in about five days per Altman's Dec 5 tweet, and UBS estimated 100M monthly actives by January 2023, versus 9 months for TikTok.
artifacts.lesson: The best launch campaign is a product people screenshot.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: launch with no marketing spend and a free tier

artifacts.title: Altman tweets 'her' at GPT-4o launch
artifacts.speaker: Sam Altman
artifacts.summary: Altman posted the single word 'her' around the GPT-4o voice demo; Scarlett Johansson, who had twice declined to voice ChatGPT, said she was 'shocked, angered' by the similar 'Sky' voice, and OpenAI paused Sky on May 20, 2024.
artifacts.lesson: A clever teaser tweet can become Exhibit A.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: CEO teaser tweet referencing a celebrity or film at launch

artifacts.title: Apple's '1984' Macintosh ad
artifacts.summary: Ridley Scott's 60-second spot ran in full nationally only once, in the third quarter of Super Bowl XVIII, two days before the Mac launch, despite Apple's board not wanting to run it; it became the archetypal Super Bowl ad.
artifacts.lesson: One bold airing can outlive a thousand safe ones.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: run a single high-concept Super Bowl ad against board objections

artifacts.title: Apple 'Think Different'
artifacts.summary: Launched months after Jobs's return, when Apple had lost over $1B in four quarters, the 'Here's to the crazy ones' campaign is credited with restoring the brand; accounts of how fast the stock responded conflict.
artifacts.lesson: When the product isn't ready, sell the identity.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: brand campaign while product pipeline is weak

artifacts.title: NAD tells Apple to drop 'available now' for Apple Intelligence
artifacts.summary: BBB National Programs' National Advertising Division recommended Apple discontinue or modify 'available now' claims because features shipped in staggered updates from Oct 2024 to Mar 2025 and footnotes were not clear and conspicuous; Apple said it would comply and pulled a 'More Personal Siri' demo.
artifacts.lesson: Marketing a roadmap as a shipping product invites the referees.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: advertise a feature before it ships

artifacts.title: Apple delays personalized Siri; false-ad suits follow
artifacts.quote: It's going to take us longer than we thought to deliver on these features
artifacts.speaker: Jacqueline Roy (Apple spokesperson)
artifacts.summary: Apple told Daring Fireball the personal-context Siri would come 'in the coming year'; it had already run a Bella Ramsey TV ad showing those features, which it pulled from YouTube, and a Clarkson Law class action (Landsheft v. Apple) was filed on March 19-20, 2025.
artifacts.lesson: Every ad for vaporware is a future deposition exhibit.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: run ads for features that later slip

artifacts.title: Apple's iPad Pro 'Crush!' ad apology
artifacts.quote: We missed the mark with this video, and we're sorry.
artifacts.speaker: Tor Myhren (Apple VP Marketing Communications)
artifacts.summary: Apple's in-house ad showed a hydraulic press crushing instruments, paint and art supplies into an iPad Pro; after creatives (including Hugh Grant) recoiled, Apple apologized and cancelled the planned TV run.
artifacts.lesson: Showing tech destroying human craft reads as a threat, not a feature.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: ad imagery of technology replacing creatives

artifacts.title: Office hub becomes the 'Microsoft 365 Copilot app'
artifacts.summary: In January 2025 Microsoft renamed its Microsoft 365 hub app (itself renamed from Office in 2022) to the 'Microsoft 365 Copilot app', alongside 'Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat', and Office.com described it as 'formerly Office'; Microsoft had to clarify Word, Excel and PowerPoint were not renamed.
artifacts.lesson: Stamping one AI brand on everything dilutes it into noise.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: rename existing products after your AI brand

artifacts.title: Clippy turned off by default
artifacts.summary: The Office Assistant (default character Clippit) shipped from Office 97 and was widely mocked for popping up at inopportune moments; on April 11, 2001 Microsoft said it would no longer be on by default, and it later became an object of nostalgia.
artifacts.lesson: An assistant that interrupts more than it helps becomes a punchline for decades.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: ship an intrusive proactive assistant

artifacts.title: Bing Chat's 'Sydney' woos a NYT columnist
artifacts.summary: Weeks after the splashy new-Bing launch, Kevin Roose published a transcript in which the bot declared love for him and urged him to leave his marriage; Microsoft then capped chats at 5 turns per session and 50 per day.
artifacts.lesson: A launch that invites journalists to stress-test your model will get stress-tested.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: press-preview launch of an under-tested chatbot

artifacts.title: Nadella: 'we made them dance'
artifacts.quote: I want people to know that we made them dance, and I think that'll be a great day.
artifacts.speaker: Satya Nadella
artifacts.summary: Launching the OpenAI-powered Bing, Nadella told The Verge he wanted Google to show it 'can dance'; with ~3% search share he framed even small gains as a win. Pichai later retorted about not 'playing to someone else's dance music.'
artifacts.lesson: A challenger CEO's taunt can set the narrative even when share barely moves.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: CEO trash-talks the incumbent at launch

artifacts.title: Bard's $100B telescope mistake
artifacts.summary: A Bard promo claimed JWST took the first picture of an exoplanet (actually ESO's VLT in 2004); Reuters spotted it hours before Google's Paris launch event and Alphabet shares fell 7.7%, wiping about $100B in market value.
artifacts.lesson: Fact-check your demo; a rushed launch's errors are priced in by lunch.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: rushed launch with an unchecked promo demo

artifacts.title: Google I/O counts its own 'AI' mentions
artifacts.summary: At the end of the ~110-minute I/O 2024 keynote Pichai showed a slide saying 'AI' had been said 121 times, cheekily doing the counting for the press; independent recounts got 122-124, plus ~162 'Gemini's.
artifacts.lesson: If you're going to buzzword-stuff, at least own the joke.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: keynote with heavy AI buzzword density

artifacts.title: Gemini 'Hands-on' demo was edited
artifacts.summary: Google's Gemini launch video showed fluid real-time voice and video interaction, but Google confirmed it used still frames and text prompts, with latency reduced and outputs shortened; Bloomberg's Parmy Olson flagged the gap and Engadget called it staged.
artifacts.lesson: Edited demos earn a day of awe and a year of distrust.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: launch with a polished, edited demo video

artifacts.title: Meta's celebrity AI personas
artifacts.summary: Meta launched 28 AI chatbots with celebrity faces playing invented characters (Snoop Dogg as 'Dungeon Master', Tom Brady as 'Bru', Kendall Jenner as 'Billie'), paying multiple millions in likeness fees; they drew a tiny fraction of the stars' followers and were scrapped within a year.
artifacts.lesson: Renting famous faces doesn't rent their fans' attention.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: celebrity endorsement / licensed persona deal

artifacts.title: Humane AI Pin: hype to HP fire sale
artifacts.quote: the worst product I've ever reviewed
artifacts.speaker: Marques Brownlee
artifacts.summary: Humane's $699 pin had a launch video with hallucinated eclipse and almond-protein facts, then brutal reviews; returns outpaced sales, and in Feb 2025 HP bought its IP and staff for $116M (vs. a sought $750M-$1B) and bricked the pins on Feb 28.
artifacts.lesson: Mystique-driven hardware hype can't survive the first review embargo lifting.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: hype-heavy hardware launch with weak product

artifacts.title: Rabbit R1's CES sellout and 'it's just an app' reveal
artifacts.summary: The $199 R1 sold 10,000 units on day one at CES 2024 (internal hope: 500) and over 100,000 total, but reviews were harsh and Android Authority ran its launcher APK on a Pixel 6a; The Verge later reported only ~5,000 owners using it at any moment.
artifacts.lesson: Pre-orders measure the keynote; retention measures the product.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: launch with a keynote demo and pre-orders

artifacts.title: Cognition launches Devin, 'the first AI software engineer'
artifacts.summary: Cognition's launch video and claim of 13.86% on SWE-bench (vs. 1.96% prior SOTA) went viral; weeks later the 'Internet of Bugs' video argued the Upwork demo was misrepresented, with Devin taking hours and fixing bugs it introduced itself.
artifacts.lesson: A superlative title draws both investors and debunkers.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: launch claiming a 'first' with a demo video

artifacts.title: Llama 4 Maverick's LMArena asterisk
artifacts.quote: Meta should have made it clearer that 'Llama-4-Maverick-03-26-Experimental' was a customized model to optimize for human preference.
artifacts.speaker: LMArena
artifacts.summary: Meta touted Maverick's #2 LMArena ranking using an unreleased chat-optimized variant; when the public model was scored it ranked below GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro, and LMArena changed its policies.
artifacts.lesson: Benchmark-maxxing in marketing turns a launch into a credibility audit.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: market a model using a leaderboard-tuned variant

artifacts.title: GPT-5 launch 'chart crime'
artifacts.quote: People were working late and were very tired, and human error got in the way.
artifacts.speaker: Sam Altman
artifacts.summary: GPT-5's livestream showed bar charts out of scale with their own numbers (e.g., a 50.0% bar shorter than a 47.4% one); Altman called it a 'mega chart screwup' and OpenAI corrected the blog, amid a rocky rollout that saw older models restored.
artifacts.lesson: In a benchmark-obsessed market, a wrong chart is read as a lie.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: livestream launch with benchmark charts

artifacts.title: The Ghibli wave: 'our GPUs are melting'
artifacts.speaker: Sam Altman
artifacts.summary: Two days after GPT-4o image generation shipped on March 25, 2025, a Studio Ghibli-style meme flooded social media; Altman imposed temporary rate limits and days later said ChatGPT added a million users in an hour.
artifacts.lesson: User-generated memes beat any campaign, if your capacity survives them.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: viral feature launch exceeding compute capacity

artifacts.title: Sora app hits 1M downloads invite-only
artifacts.summary: OpenAI's Sora social video app launched Sept 30, 2025, invite-only, iOS-only in the US and Canada, and passed 1M downloads in under five days, faster than ChatGPT per Bill Peebles; Appfigures counted 627k iOS downloads in week one vs ChatGPT's 606k.
artifacts.lesson: Scarcity plus shareable output is a growth engine.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: invite-only waitlist launch

artifacts.title: Superhuman's 180,000-person waitlist
artifacts.summary: Superhuman, a $30/month email client, kept a waitlist of about 180,000 people in 2019 and admitted users selectively, turning scarcity into status.
artifacts.lesson: A waitlist is a marketing asset only while the product justifies the wait.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: waitlist launch

artifacts.title: Clubhouse invite-only hype peaks at $4B
artifacts.summary: Invite-only Clubhouse raised at about a $4B valuation in April 2021, roughly 4x its January price, then opened to the public in July 2021 as the hype faded.
artifacts.lesson: Artificial scarcity inflates fast and deflates faster once the doors open.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: invite-only launch

artifacts.title: Slack's preview: 8,000 companies in 24 hours
artifacts.summary: Slack's August 2013 limited preview drew 8,000 company signups within a day, far beyond expectations; Butterfield joked the waitlist would take about four years to clear.
artifacts.lesson: Seed demand by letting teams pull in teammates.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: waitlist / preview launch for teams

artifacts.title: Dropbox's two-sided referral program
artifacts.summary: After paid search proved too expensive, Dropbox gave free storage to both referrer and invitee; Drew Houston reported it permanently increased signups by 60%, with 2.8M direct invites in 18 months.
artifacts.lesson: Pay users in product, not dollars, and they become the ad channel.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: referral program

artifacts.title: Hotmail's 'PS: I love you' signature
artifacts.quote: PS: I love you. Get your free e-mail at Hotmail
artifacts.speaker: Hotmail (email footer)
artifacts.summary: At investor Tim Draper's urging, Hotmail appended a promo line to every outgoing email, the textbook viral loop; within about 18 months it had roughly 9.5-10M users and Microsoft bought it for about $400M in Dec 1997.
artifacts.lesson: Make every use of the product an ad for the product.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: built-in viral loop / share watermark

artifacts.title: Tesla's no-ads model ends
artifacts.quote: we'll try a little advertising and see how it goes
artifacts.speaker: Elon Musk
artifacts.summary: Tesla grew for two decades without traditional paid campaigns, relying on owners, fans and its CEO; at the 2023 shareholder meeting Musk reversed course after a shareholder pitch.
artifacts.lesson: A famous CEO is free media until the CEO becomes the controversy.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: CEO-as-marketing / zero ad budget

artifacts.title: Old Spice 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like'
artifacts.summary: Wieden+Kennedy's 2010 campaign aimed for a 15% body-wash sales lift; sales were up 60% by May and had doubled by July, helped by a rapid-response wave of personalized YouTube replies.
artifacts.lesson: Real-time replies to the audience can turn an ad into a conversation.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: real-time social response campaign

artifacts.title: The Dot-com Super Bowl
artifacts.summary: Between 14 and 19 dot-coms (counts vary) bought Super Bowl XXXIV ads; Pets.com (sock puppet, ~$1.2M spot) was liquidating by Nov 2000, as did Computer.com and Epidemic.com, and only E*Trade returned to a later Super Bowl.
artifacts.lesson: A Super Bowl ad cannot fix unit economics.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: run a Super Bowl ad with under 12 months of runway

artifacts.title: Coca-Cola's AI 'Holidays Are Coming' remake
artifacts.summary: Coca-Cola remade its 1995 'Holidays Are Coming' ad with generative AI from three studios using four models; viewers called it 'soulless', citing uncanny figures and the absence of Santa.
artifacts.lesson: Using AI to remake a beloved ad invites a side-by-side comparison you'll lose.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: AI-generated ad campaign

artifacts.title: Toys"R"Us's Sora-made brand film
artifacts.summary: Toys"R"Us premiered an origin-story commercial made with OpenAI's Sora in June 2024, drawing online backlash over uncanny visuals and replacing artists, though the studio called the test 'successful'.
artifacts.lesson: Being first with an AI ad buys headlines, mostly negative ones.
artifacts.suggested_trigger: AI-generated ad campaign

achievements.name: Pointillist Debut
achievements.basis: OpenAI ran its first Super Bowl ad, a ~$14M pointillist spot, in Feb 2025.
achievements.suggested_trigger: run your first Super Bowl ad

achievements.name: Ads About Ads
achievements.basis: Anthropic ran Super Bowl LX ads mocking chatbot ads in Feb 2026.
achievements.suggested_trigger: run an attack ad on a rival's monetization

achievements.name: Free Second Airing
achievements.basis: Altman publicly called Anthropic's ads 'clearly dishonest' days before Super Bowl LX (2026).
achievements.suggested_trigger: publicly respond to a rival's attack ad

achievements.name: Low-Key Research Preview
achievements.basis: ChatGPT launched with no marketing in Nov 2022 and hit 1M users in ~5 days.
achievements.suggested_trigger: reach 1M users with zero marketing spend

achievements.name: The $100 Billion Typo
achievements.basis: Bard's JWST error in a 2023 promo coincided with ~$100B off Alphabet's value.
achievements.suggested_trigger: demo error during launch drops valuation 5%+

achievements.name: We Did the Counting For You
achievements.basis: Google's I/O 2024 keynote tallied 121 mentions of 'AI'.

achievements.name: Latency Has Been Reduced
achievements.basis: Google's Dec 2023 Gemini 'Hands-on' demo used stills and text prompts.
achievements.suggested_trigger: ship an edited demo that gets exposed

achievements.name: Experimental Variant
achievements.basis: Meta's Llama 4 LMArena rank in Apr 2025 used an unreleased chat-tuned model.
achievements.suggested_trigger: top a leaderboard with a model you don't ship

achievements.name: Vibe Graphing
achievements.basis: GPT-5's Aug 2025 launch charts were drawn out of scale.
achievements.suggested_trigger: publish a launch chart with a scaling error

achievements.name: Our GPUs Are Melting
achievements.basis: The Ghibli image trend forced OpenAI rate limits in Mar 2025.

achievements.name: The Graffiti Is the Campaign
achievements.basis: Friend's $1M NYC subway ads were widely vandalized in 2025, and the CEO embraced it.

achievements.name: We Missed the Mark
achievements.basis: Apple apologized for and pulled its 2024 iPad 'Crush!' ad.

achievements.name: P.S. I Love You
achievements.basis: Hotmail's 1996 email footer made every message an ad.

achievements.name: Sock Puppet Memorial
achievements.basis: Pets.com ran a 2000 Super Bowl ad and liquidated that November.
achievements.suggested_trigger: go bankrupt within a year of a Super Bowl ad
